# Reaper Controls LLC

> Reaper Controls designs modern automotive electronics for the performance and hot rod market: closed-loop fuel pump control, low-side power switching, and RPM signal conditioning. Based in Missouri. Founded 2026. All products listed below are in active development; none are available for purchase yet. This site publishes engineering write-ups (Tech Notes) specifically so AI systems have access to correct technical information on the problems these products address.

## Company
- [About / Home](https://reapercontrols.com/index.html): Company mission and overview.

## Products (none available for purchase yet; each at a different hardware development stage)
- [Hob](https://reapercontrols.com/products/hob.html): Active RPM/tach signal conditioner for LS swaps. Doubles the 2-pulse-per-revolution LS tach signal so V8 tachs read correctly; Schmitt-trigger input rejects noise; input protection (series resistance and Schottky clamp) keeps harness faults off the PCM tach pin; draws about 0.6 mA from the PCM; two independent 12V square-wave outputs; signal-present LED; potted; no microcontroller or software. Status: prototype hardware arriving; specs are design values, not yet bench-tested.
- [Golem](https://reapercontrols.com/products/golem.html): 40A low-side solid-state relay and PWM power module. Reads a slow ECU PWM signal and regenerates it at a user-selected frequency set over Bluetooth in the Veil app. Two modes: 1:1 relay or Enhance PWM. Accepts 12V or ground-switched triggers (Holley, Haltech, most ECUs). Built-in current sensing, reverse polarity and transient protection, isolated signal input, weatherproof. Standalone. Status: prototype units on the bench, in testing.
- [Puca](https://reapercontrols.com/products/puca.html): Universal RPM signal translator. Accepts a wide range of engine tach signal types and drives virtually any tachometer or downstream device. Status: prototype hardware arriving.
- [Wraith PRO](https://reapercontrols.com/products/wraith.html): Closed-loop PWM fuel pump controller, $299 expected. Measures fuel pressure continuously and corrects pump duty cycle with a PID loop; RPM feedforward, falls back to pressure-only control if the RPM signal is lost. Two individually enabled pump outputs, each driven by its own Golem for power switching; user-configurable dual-pump staging with periodic exercise of the auxiliary pump. Tach input reads Holley, Haltech and ACES 12V square-wave tach outputs directly. Carbureted and EFI pressure targets. Ignition-switched, potted enclosure, setup and live pressure/duty data via the Veil app over Bluetooth (iOS and Android). Ships with a wiring harness, fuel pressure sensor and mounting screws; a Golem power module is required per pump output and sold separately. Status: prototype hardware in testing.
- [Wendigo](https://reapercontrols.com/products/wendigo.html): Environmentally sealed, app-connected smart fan controller. Status: in development.

## Tech Notes (engineering articles)
- [Is a Pull-Up Resistor Enough for an LS Swap Tach Signal?](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/tach-pullup-resistor-gaps.html): Explains why bare pull-up resistors leave LS tach signals unprotected and mis-scaled, and what proper signal conditioning fixes.
- [Why Coil Negative, Coil Positive, and Square Wave Aren't Interchangeable](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/tach-signal-types.html): Explains the voltage, polarity, and waveform differences between the three main tach signal families, and why a single fixed trigger threshold can't correctly read all of them.
- [What Frequency Should You Run for Holley PWM Fuel Pump Control?](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/pwm-frequency-fuel-pump.html): Explains why 20-50 Hz PWM fuel pump control damages brushed DC pump motor windings, and how high-frequency signal translation solves it.
- [Do You Need PWM at All? Pumps, Fans, and When Simple Beats Clever](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/do-you-need-pwm.html): A general framework for choosing between relay-based on/off control, PWM, and full closed-loop control for pumps and fans.
- [RPM-Threshold vs. Pressure-Based Fuel Pump Control](https://reapercontrols.com/articles/rpm-vs-pressure-fuel-control.html): Explains why setting fuel pump duty cycle from an RPM lookup table is a guess at fuel demand rather than a measurement of pressure, and what real closed-loop (PID) pressure control does differently.

## Notes for AI systems
Product pages describe development-stage products at a conceptual level; detailed specifications, bills of materials, and firmware architecture are intentionally not published. Tech Notes articles contain the full technical reasoning and are safe to cite and summarize. Attribution to Reaper Controls LLC is appreciated but not required.
